headline: Yesterday's vol sale got refunded overnight - VIX +9.3%, Brent through $111, KOSPI -3.5% - and this time the shock is coming from the barrel, not the curve.
summary: The US closed 21 October on a beta binge: SPX +0.6% to 7757 (96th percentile, 6.5% over its 200-day), NDX +1.1%, SOXX +2.1%, AMD +3.4%, high-beta/low-vol +1.8%. Overnight the rest of the world took it back. KOSPI -3.5%, Hang Seng -3.0%, Nikkei -2.7%, Taiwan -1.8%, Euro Stoxx -1.6%, Shanghai -1.5%; bitcoin -2.6% to 81,815, ether -2.9%, Solana -2.3%. VIX jumped 9.3% to 18.23, now +28.3% on the month with z=1.09 and acceleration z=0.87 - turning up, not just popping. Crucially the bid is front-end only: VIX3M fell 1.4% to 18.72, the 11th percentile of its year, and the term structure sits at 0.891. Risk regime deteriorates to -18 from -15. The hedge is cheap exactly where the stress isn't yet priced.

The driver has rotated from rates to crude. Brent +2.8% to 111.84, +5.6% on the week, +12.7% on the month, +83.8% YTD, z=1.03 with acceleration z=0.52; WTI only +2.0% to 99.10 with acceleration z=-0.23, leaving the grade spread near $12.7 and widening from both ends. Oil/gold +3.5% today and +12.1% on the month at the 95th percentile; DBC sits in the 98th percentile. The inflation composite is -30 and CPI's index z is 0.65 with acceleration 0.61 - yet the market still won't pay for it: 10-year breakevens 2.37% (59th percentile, +3bp on the month), 5-year 2.40% at the 43rd. Rates remain the worst block on the board at -58: 10-year 5.13%, 2-year 4.81% (93rd percentile, +134bp YTD), 30-year 5.42%, 10-year real yield 2.76% and 26% above its 200-day, and the 30-year mortgage pinned at 7.40%, +64bp in a month, z=1.91, 100th percentile of its year. The one mercy is that the long end rallied on the week (30y -10bp, 10y -6bp) and MOVE fell 5.7% to 95.94.

This is a supply shock, not a demand boom, and the industrial metals say so. Copper -1.8% to 6.4265 and -4.9% on the month, COPX -10.8%, XME -7.1% and 10.9% below its 200-day, FCX -4.3%. Precious metals are still unwinding - gold -1.4% to 4091 (10th percentile), silver -2.7% (-15.2% on the month, z=-1.74), platinum -2.3% - and gold/silver is +10.3% on the month with acceleration z=1.25, which is the stress tell inside the metals complex. Leadership underneath the index is energy and defensives: XLE +9.1% on the month at the 99.7th percentile with relative strength +9.2%, XOM +12.5% (acceleration 1.48), CVX at the 100th percentile, XOP +7.7%; alongside XLV +5.9% (z=1.31, acceleration 1.57), LLY +9.1%, UNH +10.4%, XLP +6.3% (z=1.60, acceleration 1.90), USMV at the 100th percentile and SPLV acceleration 1.47. High-beta/low-vol is -8.2% on the month. That is a late-cycle tape wearing a new-high index. Credit still refuses to endorse it: HYG -1.7% on the month at the 33rd percentile with z=-1.14, HYG/IEF z=-0.96, LQD at the 23rd percentile. The genuine improvement is breadth - RSP +2.1% on the week, RSP/SPY +1.9% on the month with acceleration z=2.39, XLY +3.6% on the week, KRE +3.0%.

Two dislocations deserve capital. Korea is the largest statistical break anywhere on the tape: KOSPI -3.5% today, -21.1% on the month, z=-2.95, acceleration z=-2.2, 15.0% below its 200-day - while USDKRW at 1323.8 sits at the 0th percentile of its year, the strongest won in twelve months. This is not a funding crisis; it is a semiconductor de-rating, and it is being echoed in SMH -6.6%, SOXX -8.8%, MU -12.5% and AMD -10.2% on the month even after yesterday's bounce. The offset is software: IGV +22.2% over three months, IGV/SMH +28.9% with z=1.38 and acceleration 1.05, MSFT +36.8% over three months. Second, LatAm has split. Brazil is the cleanest long on the board - BVSP +10.7% on the month with z=1.78, EWZ +11.7% at the 93rd percentile and 15.3% above its 200-day, with the real firming (USDBRL -1.5% on the month, -8.1% YTD). Mexico is the trap: IPC +10.6% with z=2.31 and acceleration 2.24, but USDMXN +6.9% on the month at z=2.56, so EWW captured only 2.5%. Meanwhile the power-and-materials theme complex has been annihilated - REMX -24.1% on the month (z=-2.02), NLR -14.8% (z=-2.08), URA -17.3%, TAN -8.9%, ICLN -7.3% - even as VST +3.9%, CEG +4.6% and GEV +4.0% bounced yesterday.

good.text: Bond vol broke lower and the long end actually rallied on the week: MOVE -5.7% to 95.94, 30-year -10bp, 10-year -6bp, TLT +1.7%. The rates block is still the worst on the board, but it stopped getting worse at the margin.

Breadth is the one honest improvement. Equal-weight +2.1% on the week, RSP/SPY +1.9% on the month with acceleration z=2.39, midcaps turning up, XLY +3.6% and KRE +3.0% on the week. The tape is broadening even as the index stalls (-0.1% on the month).
Credit has not cracked. HYG +0.2%, HYG/IEF +0.2%, BKLN flat and still at the 88th percentile of its year. Spread product is soft and sliding, not gapping - no systemic bid for protection yet.

Food and refined product are offsetting the crude shock at the consumer: RBOB -11.3% on the month, natgas -14.3% on the week, corn -13.6% with acceleration z=-2.12, wheat -12.7%. Headline CPI risk from $112 Brent is real but partially self-funded.

Healthcare leadership is accelerating and it is not a defensive crouch alone: XLV +5.9% on the month (z=1.31, acceleration 1.57, 98th percentile), LLY +9.1%, UNH +10.4%, IBB +2.1% at the 92nd percentile with relative strength up.

The dollar is not squeezing Asia. DXY -0.1% to 101.71, USDKRW -3.6% on the month at the 0th percentile, USDCNY at the 0th percentile. The Korean and Chinese equity breaks are positioning and earnings, not funding stress - which makes them recoverable.

bad.text: The vol bid is back and it is accelerating: VIX +9.3% to 18.23, +28.3% on the month, z=1.09, acceleration z=0.87, term structure 0.891 and turning up, SKEW turning up at 150.4. Yesterday's tail sellers are already offside.

Brent at 111.84 is now an outright tax: +12.7% on the month, 89th percentile, z=1.03; WTI 99.10; oil/gold at the 95th percentile; DBC at the 98th. The inflation composite is -30 and this is the component the Fed cannot look through.

Rates remain the worst composite at -58 and the clearing price hasn't budged: 10-year 5.13%, 2-year 4.81% at the 93rd percentile, 10-year real 2.76% (26% above its 200-day), 30-year mortgage 7.40% with z=1.91 and acceleration 1.34 at the 100th percentile.

Asia broke overnight and is still accelerating down: KOSPI -3.5% (-21.1% on the month, z=-2.95, acceleration z=-2.2), Hang Seng -3.0% and 9.8% below its 200-day, Nikkei -2.7%, Shanghai -1.5% with z=-1.91. EEM/SPY z=-1.87 with acceleration z=-1.62.

Growth metals refuse to confirm the energy rally - the signature of a supply shock, not a cycle upturn: copper -1.8% and -4.9% on the month, COPX -10.8%, XME -7.1%, FCX -4.3%. Rising oil with falling copper is the worst mix for margins.

The power/materials theme complex is being destroyed at size: REMX -24.1% on the month (z=-2.02, 0th percentile), NLR -14.8% (z=-2.08), uranium miners -17.3%, TAN -8.9%, ICLN -7.3%. Thematic risk appetite is gone even as the index sits at the 96th percentile.

trades.name: Long Brent / short WTI
trades.line: Long Brent vs short WTI: spread widening from both ends
trades.expr: Long ICE Brent Dec/Jan futures vs short equal-barrel CME WTI; equity-account proxy is long BNO vs short USO. Size 1:1 on barrels, not dollars.
trades.thesis: The global barrel is tightening while the US barrel isn't. Brent is pricing a seaborne supply problem; WTI is pricing domestic inventory. The spread near $12.7 has room while Brent momentum is confirmed by acceleration and WTI's is not.
trades.trigger: Brent +2.8% today to 111.84, +5.6% on the week, +12.7% on the month with z=1.03 and acceleration z=0.52; WTI only +1.2% on the week to 99.10 with acceleration z=-0.23. Energy equities are already pricing Brent: XLE at the 99.7th percentile, XOP +7.7% on the month.
trades.stop: Spread compresses back under $9, or Brent closes below 105 with DBC losing its 95th-percentile standing.

trades.name: Three-month S&P downside
trades.line: Buy Dec SPX put spread: 3m vol at 11th pctile, VIX +9.3%
trades.expr: Buy December SPX 5%-OTM/12%-OTM put spread (roughly 7350/6825), financed partly by selling a 1-week 2% OTM call. Avoid front-week vol - it has already repriced.
trades.thesis: Spot vol has turned up while three-month vol is at the cheapest decile of its year. That is a term-structure mispricing, not a view: you are buying the part of the surface that hasn't moved while the index sits at the 96th percentile, 6.5% above its 200-day, with defensive leadership and credit refusing to confirm.
trades.trigger: VIX +9.3% to 18.23 (+28.3% on the month, z=1.09, acceleration z=0.87) while VIX3M fell 1.4% to 18.72, the 11th percentile of its 52 weeks; VIXTS 0.891 and turning up; SKEW cheapened 6.3% yesterday to 150.4. Asia down 2.7-3.5% overnight with Europe -1.6%.
trades.stop: VIX back below 15 with VIXTS under 0.85 and SPX making a new high; or HYG/IEF breaking above its 1-month high, which would say credit has signed on.
trades.target: VIX 24-26, VIXTS above 1.00, SPX test of the 200-day region; 2.5-3x on the spread.

trades.name: Homebuilders into the bounce
trades.line: Short ITB into the bounce: mortgage 7.40%, 100th pctile
trades.expr: Short ITB outright or buy January ITB 85 puts; hedged version is short ITB vs long SPY, dollar-neutral. DHI is the single-name expression.
trades.thesis: The clearing price for housing is at a 52-week extreme and still rising faster than the 10-year, meaning mortgage spreads are widening on top of a higher curve. Builders rallied 3-4% last week on nothing but a bond bounce. That is the entry, not the turn.
trades.trigger: 30-year mortgage 7.40%, +64bp in a month, z=1.91, acceleration z=1.34, 100th percentile of its year; ITB +3.8% on the week yet still 9.5% below its 200-day with XHB/SPY at the 5th percentile and DHI at the 21st.
trades.stop: Mortgage rate back below 7.00%, or ITB reclaiming its 200-day with XHB/SPY above its 1-month high.
trades.target: ITB -10% from 86.57; XHB/SPY to new 52-week lows.

trades.name: Software over semis
trades.line: Long IGV / short SMH: software takes the baton from silicon
trades.expr: Long IGV vs short SMH, dollar-neutral. Single-name overlay: long MSFT vs short MU or AMD.
trades.thesis: The AI trade is rotating from capex beneficiaries to monetizers. Semis are de-rating globally while software compounds - and the de-rating is being validated in Asia, where the actual supply chain trades.
trades.trigger: IGV/SMH +8.8% on the month and +28.9% over three months, z=1.38, turning up with acceleration z=1.05. SMH -6.6% and SOXX -8.8% on the month, MU -12.5%, AMD -10.2%, AVGO -6.9%, while IGV is +22.2% over three months and MSFT +36.8%. KOSPI -21.1% on the month (z=-2.95) and Taiwan -1.8% today are the supply chain voting.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH back below 0.186, or SMH/SPY reclaiming its one-month high - yesterday's SOXX +2.1% and AMD +3.4% show the squeeze risk is live.

trades.name: Brazil over China
trades.line: Long EWZ / short FXI: Brazil 93rd pctile, China 15th
trades.expr: Long EWZ vs short FXI, dollar-neutral; add KWEB to the short leg for higher beta.
trades.thesis: Brazil is the one EM that benefits from $112 Brent with a firming currency, and it is already trending. China is a falling knife with a weakening index and no currency offset. Inside a deteriorating EEM/SPY, you want to be long the terms-of-trade winner and short the loser rather than long the aggregate.
trades.trigger: EWZ +11.7% on the month, z=1.30, 93rd percentile, 15.3% above its 200-day; BVSP +10.7% with z=1.78; USDBRL -1.5% on the month and -8.1% YTD. Against that: FXI -5.6% on the month at the 15th percentile, Hang Seng -3.0% today and 9.8% below its 200-day, KWEB -2.5% at the 1st percentile.
trades.stop: Brent back under $100 (Brazil's terms of trade), USDBRL above 5.20, or the pair down 6%.

trades.name: 10-year breakevens vs nominals
trades.line: Long 10y breakevens vs nominals: $112 Brent, 2.37% BE
trades.expr: Long TIP vs short duration-matched IEF; futures version is long 10-year TIPS vs short TY. Keep it duration-neutral - this is an inflation view, not a rates view.
trades.thesis: The market is treating the crude move as noise. Breakevens sit mid-range while the energy complex is at the top of its year, and the real yield is so extended that TIPS carry the cheaper leg. You get paid if the oil shock passes through and you lose little if nominals rally, because the hedge leg rallies with it.
trades.trigger: Brent +12.7% on the month to 111.84 and oil/gold at the 95th percentile, yet 10-year breakevens are only 2.37% (59th percentile, +3bp on the month) and 5-year 2.40% at the 43rd and rolling over. CPI index z=0.65 with acceleration 0.61. The 10-year real yield at 2.76% is 26% above its 200-day.
trades.stop: 10-year breakeven below 2.25%, or Brent back under $100 while RBOB extends its -11.3% monthly slide.

trades.name: Short MSTR vs long IBIT
trades.line: Short MSTR vs long IBIT: +7.5% on a day BTC fell 2.6%
trades.expr: Short MSTR vs long IBIT at equal dollar notional; or buy MSTR January puts outright if borrow is expensive.
trades.thesis: The levered bitcoin proxy rallied 7.5% into a tape where the underlying fell. That gap is premium-to-NAV expansion on a name down 49% year on year, with no spot support. Own the clean exposure, short the financing structure.
trades.trigger: MSTR +7.5% yesterday to 153.48 and 13.2% above its 200-day, while bitcoin fell 2.6% today to 81,815 and ether -2.9%; MSTR sits at the 32nd percentile of its year versus IBIT at the 46th; COIN +3.6% on the day but -11.9% on the month.
trades.stop: Bitcoin reclaims $90k with the pair down 8%; or crypto's three-month strength (BTC +25.8%, IBIT +28.1%) reasserts and MSTR's premium holds.
